newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Friday, but buying interest was thin ahead of the weekend, traders said.

They said olein was quoted at 1,445-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but offers were also heard at 1,440 rupiah. Crude palm oil was done at 1,216 rupiah, including tax and transporation costs, at a tender in Medan on Thursday.

They said the results of a 10,500-tonne tender was announced on Friday, with 500 tonnes each to be delivered in January, February and March done at 1,091.81 rupiah/kg, 1,083.63 rupiah and 1,070 rupiah respectively, excluding tax and transporation.

Three parcels of 2,000 tonnes each to be delivered in April, May and June were done at 1,070 rupiah/kg, while another three batches of 1,000 tonnes each to be delivered over the same months were done at 1,078.50 rupiah.
"The market turned quiet in the late session as players' interest waned ahead of the weekend," one trader said.

Traders said that a statement by Beddu Amang, head of the state logistics agency BULOG, that Indonesia might import more palm olein from Malaysia if domestic prices could not be controlled lend some caution to the market.
He was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying Indonesia had taken delivery of 38,000 tonnes of the 52,000 tonnes of Malaysian olein it planned to import till January.
He said the government would import more olein from Malaysia if local prices could not be controlled, adding that the current olein price was 1,450 rupiah/kg against 1,400 a year ago.

"There seems to be some kind of a caution in his remark," one trader said. "But he has previously said that prices should not be more than 1,500 rupiah. So, we have to wait and see how the market reacts on Monday."
